key_insight: Water transport in anion exchange membranes is strongly coupled to swelling and deformation, so humidity-dependent mechanics must be modeled to predict transport accurately.
engineering_relevance: For CO2 separation membranes, accounting for diffusion, hygroscopic swelling, and viscoelastic deformation helps improve design predictions under nonuniform hydration.
method: Built a transient finite element model for water transport and membrane mechanics in Fumasep FAA-3-50.
Compared uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations.
Included concentration-dependent diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelastic response.
evidence_signal: The fully coupled model was validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and matched experiments best at intermediate hydration.
watch_item: The study indicates transport is still primarily diffusion-driven, so added mechanical coupling improves fidelity but may not dominate behavior in all operating conditions.
paper_title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
